walkthroughs.body_html: Radar gives Solar System distances. Parallax measures nearby stars. Cepheids extend the ladder to ~30 Mpc. Type Ia supernovae cover billions of light-years. Hubble's law gives the largest distances.
If a galaxy recedes at 7000 km/s and H0 ~ 70 km/s per Mpc, distance ~ 7000 / 70 = 100 Mpc ~ 326 million light-years. Larger redshift means greater distance.

Choose the method that matches the scale: parallax (nearby stars), Cepheids (galaxies in Local Group), Type Ia (distant galaxies), Hubble's law (cosmological distances). Always state assumptions and limits.
